title: Brainfile Board Schema
description: Schema for Kanban-style task boards. In v2 (per-task file architecture), the board file is config-only: it defines columns, document types, and project metadata. Tasks are standalone .md files in .brainfile/tasks/ (active) and .brainfile/logs/ (completed), each validated against task.json. In v1 (legacy), tasks are embedded in column arrays within this file.

columns.description: Board columns defining workflow stages. In v2, columns are config-only (no embedded tasks). In v1 (legacy), columns may contain a tasks array.

types.description: Additions to and overrides of the document types. epic, spec, plan, task and decision are built in and need no entry; an entry under one of their names overrides it, and any other name adds a type, optionally taking a built-in's place with like. Entries under the aliases issue and adr do not configure task or decision. In strict mode a document's type must be built in or listed here.

related.description: Sister boards in other repositories, by short name. Each value is the repository folder, relative to this repository's root (the project root, not .brainfile/). A task refers to a task on one as alias:task-id, in dependsOn or anywhere a task ID is taken. A folder that is not on this machine is still valid.

strict.description: Enables strict validation for CLI operations. When true, add rejects unknown document types, move rejects unknown columns, and add, patch and lint refuse an off-pattern parent. When false (default), unknown types and columns are allowed and an off-pattern parent is a warning. The built-in types (epic, spec, plan, task, decision) are always valid even if not listed in types.

columns.description: Column IDs to include in progress statistics

archive.description: Deprecated in v2. In v1, holds archived tasks removed from active columns. In v2, completed tasks live as individual files in .brainfile/logs/.

typeEntry.description: Configuration for a document type: a type of your own, or an override of a built-in. Defines how items of this type behave within the board.

like.description: The built-in type whose place this one takes: its parents, children, completion rule and glyph. One of epic, spec, plan, task, decision (or the aliases issue, adr), or another type on the board. Without like, a type behaves as a task.

idPrefix.description: Prefix for auto-generated IDs of this type (e.g., 'epic' produces 'epic-1', 'epic-2'). Defaults to the type name.

completable.description: Whether items of this type complete when moved to a completion column. Defaults to true, or to the like type's rule. A task is always completable; a decision never is.

schema.description: Optional JSON Schema URL for validating the extended fields of this type. Can be a remote URI (https://) or a local file path relative to the project root.

id.description: Unique column identifier in kebab-case (e.g., 'todo', 'in-progress'). Referenced by task.column in per-task files.

order.description: Display order for the column. Lower numbers appear first. Columns without order appear last.

completionColumn.description: Marks this column as a completion column. When true, tasks moved to this column are considered complete. Enables explicit completion semantics for non-English column names and custom workflows.

tasks.description: Deprecated in v2. In v1, holds tasks embedded in this column. In v2, task membership is declared via the column field in each task's frontmatter (see task.json).

task.description: Deprecated in v2. Inline task definition for v1 backward compatibility. In v2, use the standalone task.json schema instead.

effort.description: Optional effort estimation for AI planning

blockedBy.description: Optional list of item IDs that block this task

parentId.description: Optional parent task/document ID for first-class parent-child linking

dueDate.description: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format

updatedAt.description: When the task was last updated

relatedFiles.description: Optional list of related file paths or code locations

subtasks.description: Optional list of subtasks for tracking granular progress
